what: No guidance on which device query gives the per-core CB budget. ttnn.get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() is l1_end - KERNEL_CONFIG (1,531,904 B on BH) but static CBs start at the allocator base (bank 1,461,248 B); planner+implementer used the former and over-budgeted by 70.6 KB, causing CB/L1 clashes on resident-operand plans.
suggest: State in the L1 reference / memory-budget-metal skill: CB budget = ttnn.get_memory_view(dev, ttnn.BufferType.L1).total_bytes_per_bank minus any L1 buffers the op allocates; never get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size().

what: Design pattern caches op-internal L1 buffers (sharded handoff tensor, global semaphores) per plan key forever; with many distinct shapes on one mesh they accumulate and clash with later CB regions (~600 golden failures). Acceptance tests (few shapes) never see it.
suggest: Planner/CCL reference: persistent per-plan buffers only in DRAM; L1 backing buffers per call (generic_op patches dynamic CB addresses on cache hit); global semaphores keyed by transport identity (mesh, axis, links), not per shape.

what: Multi-chip golden suite takes 50-70 min, beyond the 10-min foreground tool cap, so it must be detached; killing a run mid-flight (or even a post-run reset) left BH Ethernet cores untrained and the next mesh open failed unless /tmp/tt-device.dirty was touched to force a pre-run reset.
suggest: Document the detached-run pattern for long golden suites, and have run_safe_pytest/eval_test_runner always reset before opening a fabric mesh (or detect the eth-not-active TT_THROW and reset+retry).
